title: Arrive
anchor: Nothing booked. Walk to Ameyoko and eat standing up.
notes: Drop bags, then Ueno on foot — Ameyoko is 12 minutes from the door.
大統領 for motsu-nikomi, or Kanda for soba if you land early.
Do not schedule anything. The trip is long enough.

title: Ginkgo, then Aoyama
anchor: 神宮外苑いちょう並木 at first light — Ginza line direct, no changes.
notes: Forecast peak was 26 Nov, so you're catching the tail of gold. Ginkgo holds a week or more.
Be there by 08:00. Saturday in peak season is shoulder-to-shoulder by 11:00.
カフェ香咲 is four minutes away and on the national top-100 kissaten list.
Then Philocoffea, and 櫻井焙煎研究所 for tea if you booked it.
Evening: Marunouchi and Midtown Hibiya illuminations in one loop, then a Ginza bar.

title: Yanesen on foot
anchor: 谷根千 — Nezu Shrine, Yanaka Ginza, and the cats.
notes: Maple peak is today, but every famous garden is full on a Sunday. This is the quiet alternative.
カヤバ珈琲 opens at 08:00 — get there before the queue.
Ignis in Sendagi for Panama coffee. All of it walkable from your side of town.
Dinner: Nakameguro if the sushi booking landed, otherwise Kanda.

title: Rikugien after dark
anchor: 六義園 night illumination, 18:00–20:30. Booked in advance.
notes: Mondays close Shinjuku Gyoen and most museums. Gardens and streets are the play.
Daytime: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa for Mameya Kakeru's coffee course and the garden.
巣鴨ときわ食堂 near Komagome for a top-100 shokudo dinner after the lights.
Komagome is 12 minutes on the Yamanote from Okachimachi.

title: Out of town
anchor: Kamakura — temple maples and Hasedera lit after sunset.
notes: Tuesday is the heaviest closing day for Tokyo restaurants. Being elsewhere is efficient.
Kamakura peaks late — one of the last in Japan, holding into December.
Alternative: Mt Takao, 55 min and ¥580, if you'd rather walk than look.
Take 神田志乃多寿司 inarizushi on the train.

title: Knives, then the good dinner
anchor: Booked dinner #1. Kappabashi in the morning.
notes: Kappabashi 10:30–12:00 is the quiet window. Start at 釜浅商店.
Buy today if you want engraving — 1 to 3 days.
Lunch: すぎ田 in Kuramae, top-100 tonkatsu, if you booked. Otherwise 麺 みつヰ.
Afternoon: Kiyosumi or back through Asakusa for its four top-100 kissaten.

title: Ginza and the bars
anchor: Booked dinner #2, then a proper bar.
notes: カフェ・ド・ランブル in the afternoon — aged coffee, nothing else like it in the world.
Depachika crawl at Mitsukoshi Ginza before closing.
Punch Room or Mori Bar Gran after dinner. Punch bowls suit two people.
Last chance for anything you saw and didn't buy.

title: Leave
anchor: Ameyoko for food to take home, then out.
notes: Dried fish, sesame, knives already boxed. Matsuzakaya depachika does the rest.
Knives in checked luggage. Every time.
